children.text: yadā mama pareṣāṃ ca bhayaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca na priyam /
children.translated_text: Since for myself and others, fear and suffering are not dear,

children.text: tadātmanaḥ ko viśeṣo yattaṃ rakṣāmi netaram // Śsk_1 //
children.translated_text: then what distinction is there of the self, that I protect it and not others? // <s>Śsk</s>_1 //
By one who wishes to make an end of suffering, by one who desires to reach the end of happiness,

children.text: śraddhāmūlaṃ dṛḍhīkṛtya bodhau kāryā matirdṛḍhā // Śsk_2 //
children.translated_text: having firmly established the root of faith, one should make the resolve toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) firm // <s>Śsk</s>_2 //
(Zeal in training:) The <s>bodhisattva's</s> vow arises from the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
therefore one should know the vital points by which one would be free from transgression // <s>Śsk</s>_3 //
Of one's own person, of enjoyments, of merit acquired in the three times,
the relinquishment to all beings, the protection of that, and the increase of purity // <s>Śsk</s>_4 //
One's own person and the rest are given for the enjoyment of beings;

children.text: arakṣite kuto bhogaḥ ki dattaṃ yanna bhujyate // Śsk_5 //
children.translated_text: when unprotected, how can there be enjoyment? What is given that is not used? // <s>Śsk</s>_5 //
Therefore, for the benefit and enjoyment of beings, one should protect one's person and the rest,
through not abandoning virtuous friends and through constant study of the <s>sūtras</s> // <s>Śsk</s>_6 //
In that regard, what is the protection of one's person? It is the avoidance of harm.
By what is all this attained? By the avoidance of fruitless exertion // <s>Śsk</s>_7 //
This is accomplished through constant mindfulness; mindfulness arises from intense zeal;
zeal is born from knowing the greatness of tranquility, through earnest effort // <s>Śsk</s>_8 //
The <s>Muni</s> (Sage) declared: 'One who is concentrated knows things as they truly are';

children.text: śamācca na caleccitaṃ bāhyaceṣṭā nivartanāt // Śsk_9 //
children.translated_text: and the mind should not waver from <s>śama</s> (tranquility), through the cessation of external activities // <s>Śsk</s>_9 //
One should be unshakable everywhere, through gentle and affectionate speech to those of lesser understanding,
one should attract suitable people, and one also becomes worthy of acceptance // <s>Śsk</s>_10 //

children.text: anādeyaṃ tu taṃ lokaḥ paribhūya jināṅkuram /
children.translated_text: But the world, despising the one who is unworthy of acceptance, that sprout of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),

children.text: bhasmacchanno yathā vahniḥ pacyeta narakādiṣu // Śsk_11 //
children.translated_text: like a fire covered by ashes, would be cooked in the hells and such realms // <s>Śsk</s>_11 //
In the <s>Ratnamegha</s> (Cloud of Jewels sūtra), the <s>Jina</s> has declared the concise vow:
whatever causes displeasure to beings, that one should carefully avoid // <s>Śsk</s>_12 //
This is the protection of one's person, through medicines, shelter, and such;
but from enjoying things for one's own craving, afflicted transgression arises // <s>Śsk</s>_13 //
One should act with well-begun efforts and with knowledge of proper measure in all things;

children.text: iti śikṣāpadādasya bhogarakṣā na duṣkarā // Śsk_14 //
children.translated_text: thus, from this rule of training, the protection of enjoyments is not difficult // <s>Śsk</s>_14 //
Through dispassion toward the fruit of one's own benefit, merit is well protected;

children.text: paścātāpaṃ na kurvīta na ca kṛtvā prakāśayet // Śsk_15 //
children.translated_text: one should not feel regret, and having done something, one should not publicize it // <s>Śsk</s>_15 //
One should be fearful of gain and honor, and should always avoid self-exaltation;
a <s>bodhisattva</s> should be serene and should abandon doubt regarding the <s>Dharma</s> // <s>Śsk</s>_16 //
The enjoyment of a purified person will be wholesome,
like properly prepared food free from impurities for embodied beings // <s>Śsk</s>_17 //

children.text: tṛṇacchanna yathā śasyaṃ rogaiḥ sīdati naidhate /
children.translated_text: Just as grain covered by weeds is afflicted by diseases and does not flourish,

children.text: buddhāṅkurastathā vṛddhiṃ kleśacchanno na gacchati // Śsk_18 //
children.translated_text: so the sprout of <s>Buddha</s>-nature, covered by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), does not grow // <s>Śsk</s>_18 //
What is the purification of one's person? It is the cleansing of sins and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);
through the essence of the purpose of the <s>samyak-sambuddha</s> (fully awakened one), without effort one falls into lower realms // <s>Śsk</s>_19 //
One should be patient, one should seek learning, one should then take refuge in the forest,
one should apply oneself to <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), and one should cultivate contemplation of the impure and so forth // <s>Śsk</s>_20 //
One should understand the purification of enjoyments through the purification of right livelihood;
from actions rooted in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), comes the purification of merit // <s>Śsk</s>_21 //

children.text: grahītāraḥ subahavaḥ svalpaṃ ceda manena kim /
children.translated_text: The recipients are very many, and what is given is small — what use is pride?
And since this does not produce excessive satisfaction, it should therefore be increased // <s>Śsk</s>_22 //
What is the increase of one's person? It is the increase of strength, diligence, and energy;
from giving rooted in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) comes the increase of enjoyments // <s>Śsk</s>_23 //
Having first made firm one's resolution and intention through effort,

children.text: karuṇāṃ ca puraskṛtya yateta śubhavṛddhaye // Śsk_24 //
children.translated_text: and placing <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) foremost, one should strive for the increase of virtue // <s>Śsk</s>_24 //
The practice of the <s>Bhadracaryā</s> (Noble Conduct) should be performed — prostrations and the rest — with zeal;
constant practice of faith and the other virtues, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> and others // <s>Śsk</s>_25 //
In all circumstances, the welfare of beings, the gift of <s>Dharma</s> without material motive,

children.text: bodhicittaṃ ca puṇyasya vṛddhihetuḥ samāsataḥ // Śsk_26 //
children.translated_text: and <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) — these are, in brief, the causes for the increase of merit // <s>Śsk</s>_26 //
Success in the <s>samyak-prahāṇas</s> (right exertions) comes from not separating from diligence,
through mindfulness, through <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension), and through wise reflection // <s>Śsk</s>_27 //
